speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I have heard from Minister Jeffrey Siow that connecting to the Cross Island Line is a possibility, but currently, it is still very congested and honestly, connectivity in Jalan Kayu Fernvale can be improved.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I understand the complexities, but can we have a more definitive timeline?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: After all, it has been six years since the studies have begun.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: The second supplementary question is: in the meantime, would the Ministry of Transport (MOT) be putting in better bus connectivity?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: While I understand it is not the most efficient, this would be needed for the long interim.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I know he is very, very concerned for his Jalan Kayu residents and also, residents in the North East area.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will first say that rail projects, as we all know, are major public investments and they do require careful consideration of a variety of factors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This include current and future land use needs, and that is why we also need to look at engineering feasibility and also potential environmental impacts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have to work with the relevant planning agencies to assess the demand and the implementation timeline of the project so as to be able to support existing and future developments along the corridor, as well as sourcing for suitable sites for a train depot, which are large facilities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is followed by detailed engineering studies to ascertain the engineering feasibility and the appropriate corridor and station locations to maximise the catchment while trying to minimise inconveniences and disruptions as much as possible, during the construction phase.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are already doing this as quickly as we can, but at the same time, are making sure that no stones are left unturned.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are working in close consultation with other land use agencies such as the Urban Redevelopment Authority, the Housing and Development Board, and JTC.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And we will be sharing more details as we are progressively identifying and introducing these enhancements.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have filed a PQ on the Seletar Line for subsequent Sitting, so I will just ask my supplementary question today.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I understand that feasibility studies are still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Given that the NEL overcrowding issues are quite bad already today, and I understand the Cross Island Line is upcoming, but the proposed routing for the Seletar Line is likely to be more of a direct parallel and provide more direct loading relief for the NEL.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, given that, will the Ministry consider accelerating the timeline of the Seletar Line's development?
